stages.title: Demand-side policy: strengths, weaknesses and conflicts
stages.sub: After this stage the student can explain how monetary policy's speed and fiscal policy's cost create conflicts between policies and objectives.

steps.q: The Monetary Policy Committee meets every month and can change interest rates almost immediately after deciding to. A government budget, by contrast, is usually only set once a year. Which policy can respond faster to new economic data?
steps.right: Monetary policy, because the MPC meets often
steps.wrong: Fiscal policy, because it covers more of the economy
steps.hint: Think about how often each body actually meets and can act.

steps.q: A government wants to cut unemployment by running a budget deficit, spending more than it raises in tax. At the same time it has promised voters it will keep tax revenue and spending equal. Can it do both at once?
steps.right: No, running a deficit breaks the balanced budget goal
